subject: Orchard Bank security qualification — post-call debrief and artifact asks
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@orchardbank.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Orchard Bank security qualification — post-call debrief and artifact asks

Maya — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our end and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of pain & goals (what you stated)
- Audit log retention requirement: 7 years for transactional events and 3–5 years for non-transactional traces.
- SOC 2 attestation required for production access; you’ll need either current report (within 12 months) or an attestation timeline.
- Pen test evidence: you need a vendor-validated pen test from the last 12 months and remediation notes.
- DPA concerns: specific clauses around data residency, subprocessor list, and audit rights.

What Redwood can provide (today)
- SOC 2 Type II report copy or SOC 3 summary (we'll confirm exact scope)
- Audit log schema doc + retention configuration steps (we keep pluggable retention policies per account)
- Pen-test summary & remediation log (redacted where necessary)
- Draft DPA for legal review (we attached a working PDF)

Immediate next steps / owners
1) Redwood to send SOC 2 checklist and evidence matrix — Alex (target: EOD Thu, Aug 13)
2) Redwood legal to drop initial DPA redlines — Alex will share redwood-dpa-draft.pdf (attached)
3) Orchard to confirm exact retention timeframe and any regulatory citations that require 7 years — Maya / Rajesh (target: Thu Aug 13)
4) Schedule a short follow-up (30 min) with security + platform to walk audit-log mapping and encryption details — Jonas to propose slots (target: week of Aug 17)

Attachments included: OrchardBank_SOC2_Checklist.xlsx (artifact matrix), redwood-dpa-draft.pdf (working DPA)

Questions for you now:
- Can you confirm whether the 7-year retention applies to full message payloads or transaction metadata only?
- Are there any specific pen-test vendors or certification formats you prefer (CREST, OSSTMM, etc.)?

If that matches your read of the call, we’ll open a mutual action plan in HubSpot and lock dates. Thanks — looking forward to keeping this moving.

—
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
[Attachment: OrchardBank_SOC2_Checklist.xlsx (Excel, 28KB)]
[Attachment: redwood-dpa-draft.pdf (PDF, 112KB)]

From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@orchardbank.com>

Cc: Rajesh Iyer <rajesh.iyer@orchardbank.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 17:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Orchard Bank security qualification — post-call debrief and artifact asks

Alex — thanks for the clear summary. That aligns with our notes. A few clarifications: 

1) Retention scope: the 7-year requirement is for transaction payloads and any data necessary to reconstruct transactional flows for audit/regulatory purposes. Metadata retention (request IDs, timestamps) can be shorter (we discussed 5 years as minimal).
2) SOC2: we prefer a full Type II report when available; otherwise a current interim SOC 2 plus an attestation timeline is acceptable.
3) Pen test: no hard vendor requirement but we typically look for CREST-aligned reports or equivalent; a remediation timeline with CVE references is required.

I’m attaching our vendor security scorecard template for reference so you can see how we map artifacts to controls.

Action: I’ll confirm our retention legal language and send it back by Thursday morning. For the meeting on logs, can Jonas do Aug 18 between 9–11am PT?

Thanks — Maya
Maya Patel
Head of Vendor Risk | Orchard Bank
maya.patel@orchardbank.com | +1 (202) 555-0148

Also note: if Orchard requires a 7-year retention for payloads, we should flag potential storage cost delta and propose a lifecycle policy with cold storage + archive export options. I’ll draft a short cost estimate after Alex shares artifact mapping.
